messages:
maria: heads up - apac1 dedicated pool-7 is reporting ~55% of GPUs unreachable, cluster health alerts firing. I see a bunch of PLEG and node_ready flaps.
sean: ack, seeing the same. Which AZ?
maria: it's AZ-c primarily. netops alerted to switch-level errors earlier.
jay: Observed sudden increase in pod eviction events + kubelet connection resets. logs: `kubelet: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing`
katie: deploy-bot reported a failed drain: `drain node pool-7-node-12: timeout waiting for pod termination`
ben: traffic is already overflowing to hosted routing? monitoring shows the weighted-routing shift kicked in at 10:05 UTC -> hosted weight +40% for that org tier.
maria: correct. I manually bumped hosted weight to 60% for dedicated-pool-7 orgs to avoid 503s while we triage.
sean: what triggered autoscaler? are we OOMing replacement nodes?
jay: autoscaler is healthy but cloud quota for GPUs in apac1 is at soft limit. it can't allocate replacements, so pods stay pending.
katie: cost note: hosted absorption will add ~15-20k USD/day if sustained at this level. need gating rules for non-critical jobs.
maria: immediate plan: 1) maintain hosted weight at 60% (done), 2) set low-priority throttle for background batches (call it `lp-throttle: 30r/s`), 3) open cloud quota request, 4) try controlled node reboot of 4 affected nodes after midnight local.
sean: I'll push lp-throttle for orgs tagged `non-prod,batch` now. command: `/infra rate-limit set --org-tags non-prod,batch --rps 0.5`
deploy-bot: rate-limit change queued: non-prod,batch -> 0.5rps. will apply in 12s.
jay: trying a soft reboot sequence for node-12 and node-15 in AZ-c. I'll cordon -> drain -> reboot. doing node-12 now: `kubectl cordon node-12 && kubectl drain node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`
katie: notify customer success for any potential latency spikes for enterprise customers in apac1. cc @product-ops
ben: quick thought — we can do a temporary routing rule: prefer dedicated->hosted fallback only for interactive (latency-sensitive) routes, queue batch ops entirely to hosted to preserve tokens on hosted instead of dedicated. reduces cross-customer noise.
maria: good. ben, can you write the routing patch? small HCL snippet is fine.
ben: patch ready, pushing to canary: `route.apac1.override { match: route.type == "batch" -> weight: hosted: 100, dedicated: 0 }`
jay: node-12 reboot finished, kubelet re-registered, pods rescheduled. health: node-12 Ready.
sean: node-15 still failing to come back, appears stuck at `kernel: mlx5_core FW error` from switch driver. netops investigating.
katie: if netops can't confirm fix in 30m, suggest expanding hosted weight to 75% and schedule a dedicated drain window tonight.
maria: agreed. I'm creating an incident PRD with timeline + cost estimate and mitigation actions.
ben: also adding an alert to cost-ops to watch daily hosted spend delta.
jay: reminder - when we shift more weight to hosted, KV-cache cold-starts will increase per-token latency. we should disable long tail caching for batch routes to avoid memory pressure on hosted nodes.
maria: noted. action items: (maria) incident doc + customer comms, (sean) lp-throttle apply and validate, (ben) routing patch canary, (jay) finish node-15 troubleshooting + coordinate netops, (katie) CS notif. Re-evaluate in 25m.
sean: lp-throttle applied and validated for 85% of targets. latency for interactive routes stable so far.
eta: 25m check-in scheduled 1729456320.
maria: thanks team. keeping thread open for updates.
deploy-bot: automated reminder: next scheduled action -> increase hosted weight to 75% at 10:38 UTC if no resolution detected.
